title: Subnet News — August 12, 2026
summary: Engy replaced its disputed blanket whitelist with dual permissionless and enterprise onboarding, while Iota rotated security after a drained-wallet attack and Score launched daily private-track audits. Beam broadened its proposed emission distribution, and Hone, Ditto, BASE, Trishool, Bitsec and NIOME advanced scoring or protocol releases. Slightly fewer than half of subnet markets rose, with OpenRoboto leading credible gains and Prometheon, Enclave, Engy and RedTeam leading declines. No supported future alpha unlock was found.

highlights.headline: Fewer than half of subnet markets rise as rotation stays sharp
highlights.summary: At the 11:09 AM ET snapshot, 61 directional subnet markets rose and 65 fell, with about 89,966 TAO of reported 24-hour volume. OpenRoboto led credible gainers at +10.5%; Prometheon, Enclave, Engy and RedTeam led declines. An invalid SN70 print was excluded.

highlights.headline: Short-window liquidity rotates into Synth and Babelbit
highlights.summary: Over the latest hour, Synth added about 416 TAO to its pool, Babelbit about 127 TAO, KubeTEE about 70 TAO, OpenRoboto about 61 TAO and Bitsec about 60 TAO. Bitcast lost about 146 TAO, Enclave about 40 TAO and BASE about 27 TAO. These are descriptive pool-reserve changes, not inferred investor intent.

updates.headline: Required v3 protocol upgrade scheduled for 22:00 UTC
updates.summary: Hone announced a breaking v3 release adding explicit Python and Rust problem support and setting owner burn to zero. Coordinated miner and validator upgrades are required; this was an announced deployment at the report cutoff, not yet a completed rollout.

updates.headline: Team responds to drained-wallet attack
updates.summary: Iota said a drained-wallet incident is under investigation and that infrastructure security is being rotated. Orion 16B payouts moved to manual processing while the incident response continues.

updates.headline: Universal jailbreak challenge format launches
updates.summary: Trishool introduced one reusable jailbreak template evaluated across multiple objectives, alongside a guard-model update and scoring reset. The format is live according to the team brief; performance outcomes remain to be measured.

updates.headline: Daily private-track audit system goes live
updates.summary: Score will randomly publish daily audit samples from top private-track performers, including miner responses and evaluation evidence. The public repository also merged per-element audit storage work during the window.

updates.headline: Stake-lock display bug identified
updates.summary: Nepher explained that small conviction-lock adjustments could appear to have no effect because perpetual and decaying lock buckets interact during roll-forward. The team described the issue as a display/accounting-path bug, not a token cliff.

updates.headline: Dual mining onboarding replaces blanket whitelist
updates.summary: Following the previous day's backlash, Engy described two paths: permissionless TEE onboarding for supported frontier models and a vetted enterprise track. The team also announced a buyback program. The policy direction is confirmed; execution and buyback scale remain team-reported.

updates.headline: Version 3 targeted for mainnet this week
updates.summary: NIOME said v3 is moving from testnet to mainnet this week after workflow stabilization. The team said emissions will reward top-performing miners; the exact activation block was not published at the cutoff.

updates.headline: Provenance fix prepared after fingerprint failure
updates.summary: Bitsec identified a fingerprinting failure affecting validator scoring and said a provenance fix would ship before the next round to make simple copycat strategies less effective.

updates.headline: Kimi K3 outage resolved
updates.summary: Chutes restored Kimi K3 after a miner outage. Users continued reporting material performance variance across several models, so availability was restored but quality concerns remained open.

updates.headline: PRISM weight-sealing bug fixed
updates.summary: BASE merged a fix for weights being sealed against results from a different epoch and instructed miners to update. This is a required participant update tied to scoring correctness.

updates.headline: Emission distribution broadens to 30 UIDs
updates.summary: Beam discussed expanding rewarded miners from the top 20 to the top 30 and clarified that PRISM bandwidth scoring is constrained by the slowest chunk in a batch. The change broadens participation while retaining performance gates.

updates.headline: Hardcoded miner blocklist dispute escalates
updates.summary: A developer challenged hotkey restrictions visible in Minotaur's code as unfair; the team defended them as anti-spam enforcement. The policy is visible and disputed, but the surrounding allegations were not independently adjudicated.

updates.headline: v9 activates with post-release fixes underway
updates.summary: Ditto activated benchmark v9 but found bugs requiring another test cycle. The team is rerunning leading v8 agents to trigger v9 incentives while validator instability continues to delay scores.

updates.headline: Benchmark trajectories published through Hippius
updates.summary: Affine's public repository added per-task benchmark rollout records, trajectory publishing to Hippius, and a metrics page during the window, providing verifiable development activity beyond team chat.

ecosystem.headline: Emission gate keeps concentrating the tape
ecosystem.summary: Chutes, lium, Affine, Targon and Score remained the largest emission recipients at the snapshot. GM's one-hour emission share fell about 0.24 percentage points, while other tracked changes were much smaller. Miner-burn data is embedded in the protocol's price-and-burn allocation formula, but a complete per-subnet burn table was not publicly recoverable for the cutoff.

ecosystem.headline: Conviction remains concentrated without a verified unlock event
ecosystem.summary: MVTRX had 27.7% of displayed supply conviction-locked, followed by Swarm at 22.4%, DSperse at 20.8% and Bitsec at 19.9%. No direct announcement or identifiable chain event supported a future dated alpha unlock. Decaying locks release continuously rather than at a guaranteed cliff.

ecosystem.headline: No verified alpha halving or slot replacement in the window
ecosystem.summary: The sweep found no supported subnet alpha halving and no clearly attributable registration/deregistration event. SN70's feed produced an impossible 781% change with negative volume and was treated as a data anomaly, not a market or slot event.

gaps: Public X indexing returned no reliable comprehensive result set for the historical query groups; inaccessible, deleted, private and login-gated posts could not be exhaustively reviewed.
Many original Discord messages require Bittensor server membership or login; SubnetRadar briefs that preserve direct message links were used when the originals were inaccessible.
SN70 returned an impossible +781% 24-hour move with negative volume and was excluded from rankings pending backend correction.
The live screener exposes exact one-hour pool-reserve changes but not a complete historical 24-hour reserve series; flow examples are labeled as one-hour changes.
A complete per-subnet miner-burn concentration table and historical conviction mode-change log were not publicly recoverable at the cutoff.
No direct project announcement or identifiable on-chain evidence supported a future dated alpha unlock, so upcomingUnlocks is empty.
No material public update was verified for subnets with empty update arrays. This report is informational and not financial advice.
